input.question: Why did the military claim that a a flying saucer crashed at Roswell?
input.ground_truth: According to the US government narrative, a rancher [ran across some classified programs](_URL_0_). And it all got out of hand because a local US Air Force press officer saw some stuff he shouldn't have and reported it as flying saucer debris. There are some pretty questionable issues with that story, and 60 years of a theoretical ecosystem centered around Roswell and UFOs and aliens, but that was the official line.

Question: Why did the military claim that a a flying saucer crashed at Roswell?

Okay, let’s imagine you have a really cool toy spaceship. One day, your toy spaceship "crashes" in your backyard. You tell your friends, and they get excited and want to see it. At first, you just say, “It’s just my toy,” but your friends want a bigger story, so you say, “Maybe it’s from outer space!”

Now, imagine the military is like a group of grown-ups who take care of everyone’s safety. When people heard about the crashed spaceship, the military said, “That’s our toy now!” and told everyone it was just a weather balloon (which is like a big balloon that helps them know the weather). But later, people thought maybe they were hiding the truth and that it was really a spaceship from another planet.

So, the military said it was just a weather balloon to keep things simple and not make everyone worry or get too excited. But some people didn’t believe them and thought it was a flying saucer from outer space!
